args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (unhealthy, error rate 18% across us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rolled back in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging prior to the production rollout. Follow-up: root-cause v2.3.1 and review why an unhealthy RC was promoted.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in every region and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks with an 18% error rate in us-east, us-west and eu-west. I rolled all three back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. A status check afterwards shows v2.3.0 running in all three regions, marked healthy, with a 0.2% error rate.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-up work. I created it at the same time as the post-rollback check, so it was written before the recovery was confirmed and doesn't mention it.

The release history shows the v2.3.1 test build was also unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. I added this to the incident as a follow-up, along with finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
